hldContextSlice.frameworkSummary: The Epic re-expresses the shipped JetBrains settings + nested-pages surface on the VS Code side as two net-new injectable seams layered over the extension's existing sc1-sc7 contracts, following the exact S001-S006 convention: small VS-Code-free cores behind injected boundaries, with extension.ts the SOLE 'vscode' importer and every core unit-testable off the editor API via node:test. Editable config lives in native VS Code Settings (a statically-declared, machine-scoped contributes.configuration for the stable global + fixed per-role keys) driven by ONE ConfigSync engine that keeps the native surface truthful to the daemon (pull on activation/refresh, live-push each change with pre-flight validate and revert-on-reject). The read-only Daemon/Workflows/Debug pages and the per-repo editor live behind ONE WebviewPanelHost (a tabbed Detailed Status panel + a separate Repo Configuration panel) fed by a read-only DaemonData gateway over the existing daemon IPC. Everything reaches the daemon only through the existing config.catalog/config.write + read IPC via sc1; no new daemon capability is added.

consumedContracts.name: ConfigSync
consumedContracts.purpose: The single VS-Code-free engine that keeps the native contributes.configuration surface truthful to the daemon: maps the config.catalog schema onto the statically-declared global + per-role keys, pulls daemon values into settings on activation/refresh, and on each native change diffs against the last-synced snapshot, pre-flight-validates, writes via config.write, and reverts to last-known-good on rejection. Consumed by every config-track story so the k5 invariant lives in one place.

boundary.internal: How the fixed RoleId taxonomy is enumerated into per-role tier-override keys and rendered as enum (core/mid/cheap) native settings, and how a role's effective tier (default vs override, clamped by coreFloor) is displayed. Consumes sc8 for the actual apply/truthful-sync; adds no new contract.

adjacentBoundaries.internal: The exact set of stable global config keys declared in contributes.configuration (machine scope) and the mapping from config.catalog paths to those native keys; the last-synced snapshot representation; and the internal validate→write→revert mechanics of the ConfigSync engine. Only the sc8 ConfigSyncEngine + its injected boundary types are exposed; how the pull and the per-change diff are computed is private.

The toast + auto-revert UX on a rejected write (the loop-suppression while reverting), the reconcile-on-activation and the 'Refresh insrc settings' durable command that drives sc8.pullFromDaemon, and the insrc.advanced escape-hatch handling. Consumes sc8; owns no shared contract.

The status-bar item's 2-item QuickPick menu, the concrete Webview panel lifecycle (create/reveal/dispose), the in-panel tab framework + host↔webview postMessage protocol, the durable palette commands for both panels, and the DaemonDataGateway's concrete IPC/log/process-scan wiring. Only the sc9 WebviewPanelHost + DaemonDataGateway types are exposed; the panel HTML/messaging internals are private.

The Daemon status view and the Workflows chain-report rendering inside their tabs, and each view's on-demand refresh control (open/tab-switch/manual). Consumes sc9's host + gateway; adds no new contract and does no background polling.

The Debug tab: the MCP-clients list rendering, the continuous polling-ticker live log tail (rotation-aware, the only continuously-refreshing view), and the consent-gated orphan-process cleanup (via the shipped sc4 ConsentGate before any kill). Consumes sc9; the ticker + confirm UX are private.

The Repo Configuration panel's repo picker (populated from sc9's registeredRepos) and the per-repo overrides editor form, plus its own per-repo config writes over the existing sc1 config.write and its inline write-feedback. Consumes sc9 for the panel host + repo list; the form layout + per-repo write handling are private.

hldContextSlice.rolloutPhase: Phase B — Config editing complete (per-role + truthful sync)

nonFunctional.performance: Panel and settings reads run off the UI path with bounded socket timeouts; Daemon/Workflows refresh only on open/tab-switch/manual (no background polling), and only the Debug log tail runs a continuous ticker. Activation is never blocked — the config pull-sync and every panel load degrade gracefully when the daemon is unreachable.
nonFunctional.security: No cloud path and no secrets (k2); all config + status access is over the local Unix-socket IPC via sc1. The only daemon-mutating action (orphan-kill) is consent-gated via the shipped sc4 before it runs (k4). Native config keys are machine-scoped so config is never carried off the machine by Settings Sync (k7).
nonFunctional.observability: Every surface reflects daemon-derived state truthfully: a rejected config write shows the daemon's reason and reverts, external changes reconcile on refresh (k5), and status/consent outcomes surface through the existing sc2 StatusSurface + getLogger (never console).
nonFunctional.durability: The daemon's ~/.insrc/config.json is the single source of truth; the native Settings mirror and all panels are stateless views/editors over it — no shadow config store. Per-repo overrides are keyed to the daemon's own repo registry (k7), independent of open workspace folders; panel state is ephemeral and rebuilt from the daemon on each open.

dataModelChanges.details: One machine-scoped native ENUM setting per fixed role (30 keys): id `insrc.models.tasks.` + roleId, type 'string' + enum ['cheap','mid','core'], default = the role's defaultTier, markdownDescription naming the role + its criticality, scope:'machine' (k7). Added as new configuration section(s) alongside S001's 7 global sections; the manifest is generated FROM reasoningRoleTaxonomy() so it cannot drift (contract-tested).

A pure VS-Code-free table built from reasoningRoleTaxonomy(): for each role, the native key `insrc.models.tasks.<roleId>`, the write SEGMENTS ['models','tasks',roleId], and a synthetic enum ConfigOption (default = defaultTier). Merged into the engine's key map so the ONE engine's pull/apply drives per-role keys 1:1. Private to S002 but shaped as S001's ConfigKeyEntry.

Add two OPTIONAL fields so the ONE engine handles both global and per-role keys without special-casing: `segments?: readonly string[]` (when present, the engine writes via ConfigGateway.writeKeyPath(segments,...) instead of writeKey(path,...)) and `source?: 'catalog' | 'raw'` (default 'catalog'; 'raw' pulls the current value from ConfigGateway.rawConfig() at the segment path instead of the catalog snapshot). S001's global entries omit both (default behavior unchanged). Additive, non-breaking to S001.
dataModelChanges.schemaDiff: interface ConfigKeyEntry { nativeKey: string; path: string | readonly string[]; option: ConfigOption; segments?: readonly string[]; source?: 'catalog' | 'raw'; }

dataModelChanges.details: S002 WRITES this dynamic per-role override path (a TierName) via the array-segment form — it must preserve the daemon invariant that models.tasks[roleId] is a flat key whose id may contain dots (src/config/analyze.ts roleTiers parse). Writing via a dot-split string would mis-nest and silently no-op (write-path.ts). The effective-tier semantics (roleTiers[role] ?? defaultTier, clamped by coreFloor for critical roles) are the daemon's and are NOT re-implemented here — S002 only presents + writes the raw per-role tier.

interactionWithShared.howDetails: S002 CONSUMES the sc8 ConfigSyncEngine (owned by S001) and drives the 30 per-role enum keys through the SAME engine so the k5 truthful-apply invariant stays in one place. It requires the two additive sc8 gateway methods proposed as an HLD amendment (writeKeyPath for dot-safe segment writes + rawConfig over config.show for the current per-role value — exactly the per-role segmentation S001's contractDetails deferred to S002), plus the additive ConfigKeyEntry.segments/source fields so the engine routes per-role keys to writeKeyPath + rawConfig while global keys keep writeKey + catalog. extension.ts (sole 'vscode' importer) merges the PerRoleKeyMap into the engine's key map and the existing onDidChangeConfiguration('insrc') listener already fans every insrc.* change (incl. insrc.models.tasks.*) to applyChanges. NO scope from S001 (the global engine internals), s3 (revert/Refresh UX), or the panel track is re-designed — only sc8 is extended, additively, within its stated 'global + per-role keys' purpose. config.show + the string[] form of config.write already exist (no new daemon capability, k3).

errorCases.response: writeKeyPath is NOT called; the change is reported as a rejected write via the Notifier with a client-authored reason ('must be one of: cheap, mid, core'); the snapshot is not advanced. The full toast/auto-revert UX is s3's — S002 only surfaces + does not persist the bad value.
errorCases.userImpact: The invalid tier never reaches the daemon (so the role would not silently fall back with no feedback); the user sees why it was rejected.

errorCases.scenario: The daemon is unreachable when the per-role pull runs (activation/refresh) — config.show rejects.

errorCases.response: No settings writes for the per-role keys (the native mirror keeps its last-known values); surfaced non-blocking via Notifier; never throws, so activation proceeds (k1 preserved).
errorCases.userImpact: The per-role settings show their last-synced (or default = defaultTier) values instead of live ones; a later refresh re-syncs. No data loss.

errorCases.scenario: config.write refuses the per-role write ({ok:false}) or the daemon drops mid-write.
errorCases.detection: ConfigGateway.writeKeyPath resolves { ok:false } (empty/invalid segment) or the rpc rejects (socket error) — sc8 inspects the ConfigWriteResult / catches the rejection, identically to the global writeKey path.
errorCases.response: Reported as a rejected write ('daemon refused' / 'daemon unreachable') via Notifier; the snapshot is not advanced for that role key.
errorCases.userImpact: The per-role edit is not silently accepted; the user is told the daemon rejected it (and via s3 it reverts). UI stays consistent with the daemon.

errorCases.scenario: The declared insrc.models.tasks.<roleId> manifest keys drift from the daemon's reasoningRoleTaxonomy() role registry (a role added/renamed/removed daemon-side).

At RUNTIME the engine is drift-safe: a native key with no PerRoleKeyMap entry is ignored, and a raw models.tasks override with no matching role key is skipped during pull.
errorCases.response: Build fails on drift (caught before shipping); at runtime an unknown role key is skipped rather than mis-written, so a version-skew daemon never corrupts config via an unknown role.
errorCases.userImpact: A drifted role simply doesn't appear/apply until the manifest is regenerated from the taxonomy; no wrong write.

alternativesConsidered.name: Flat per-role enum keys + reuse the sc8 engine via a minimal segment/raw-read extension
alternativesConsidered.oneLineSummary: Declare one static machine-scoped enum key `insrc.models.tasks.<roleId>` per fixed role (values cheap|mid|core, default = the role's defaultTier), and drive them through the SAME S001 ConfigSyncEngine after minimally widening sc8 to (a) carry array-segment write paths and (b) read the current per-role value from config.show.
alternativesConsidered.approach:
Enumerate the 30 fixed roles from reasoningRoleTaxonomy() into a static PerRoleKeyMap of ConfigKeyEntry-shaped rows: nativeKey `insrc.models.tasks.<roleId>`, the write path as literal SEGMENTS ['models','tasks',roleId] (dot-safe for dotted roleIds), and a validator/option enforcing the tier enum {cheap,mid,core} with default = role.defaultTier. These 30 keys are declared statically in package.json contributes.configuration (scope:'machine', enum), exactly like S001's global keys, and are covered by a manifest<->role-taxonomy contract test.

To drive them through the ONE sc8 ConfigSyncEngine (keeping the k5 invariant in one place), S002 makes two minimal, S001-sanctioned extensions to sc8: (1) widen ConfigKeyEntry.path and ConfigGateway.writeKey to accept `string | readonly string[]` so a dotted roleId writes via the array form through config.write (the daemon already accepts string[]); (2) add a gateway read for the current per-role value over the EXISTING config.show IPC (config.catalog.values omits dynamic models.tasks.*), so pullFromDaemon can mirror the daemon's actual override (or the role's defaultTier when unset). The engine gains a tiny per-entry 'source' notion (catalog value vs raw config.show) so global keys keep pulling from catalog and per-role keys pull from raw. Everything else (validate, write-once, idempotent no-op, snapshot, never-throw) is reused unchanged.
pros: Native VS Code per-field editing for every role (enum dropdown cheap/mid/core, inline description, search) — directly satisfies ac1/ac2's 'editable choice' value, mirroring the JetBrains PerRoleSection.
Keeps the k5 truthful-apply invariant in the ONE sc8 engine (the HLD's stated intent), reusing S001's validated pull/validate/write/snapshot machinery instead of duplicating it.

The two sc8 extensions are exactly the segmentation + per-role read S001's contractDetails EXPLICITLY deferred to S002, and add NO new daemon capability (config.show + the string[] form of config.write already exist, k3).
Static key set + a manifest<->role-taxonomy contract test catches drift at build if the role registry changes.
cons: Touches S001-owned sc8 code (writeKey/path signature widening + a new gateway read + a per-entry source branch) — must be documented as a sanctioned consume-and-extend and confirmed at approval (possible HLD back-flow if judged a contract change).
30 more declared manifest keys (the role registry is large), a bigger contributes.configuration block.

The 'native value == defaultTier' case is ambiguous (override vs no-override); S002 must define the write/remove semantics for a value equal to the default (deferring the full remove-override UX richness to native Reset Setting).

alternativesConsidered.name: Flat per-role keys driven by a SEPARATE S002-owned per-role sync core
alternativesConsidered.oneLineSummary: Same static per-role enum keys, but S002 builds its own per-role sync core (its own gateway + apply/pull) calling config.show/config.write directly via sc1, leaving S001's sc8 engine untouched.
alternativesConsidered.approach: Declare the same 30 static `insrc.models.tasks.<roleId>` enum keys, but instead of extending sc8, S002 introduces a parallel VS-Code-free core (e.g. createPerRoleSync) over its own thin gateway that reads config.show and writes the segment-array form of config.write. It re-implements the validate + last-synced-snapshot + never-throw + idempotent-no-op logic for the per-role key set, and extension.ts wires a second onDidChangeConfiguration path (or the same listener fanning per-role keys to this core).
pros: Zero change to S001-owned sc8 code — clean ownership boundary, no back-flow question.
The per-role core can specialize freely (segment writes, config.show reads, coreFloor-aware display) without generalizing sc8.
cons: DUPLICATES the k5 truthful-apply logic (validate/write/snapshot/never-throw) that the HLD says must live in ONE place ('the k5 invariant lives in one place'; 'consumed by every config-track story') — two engines to keep behaviourally identical, a real drift/consistency hazard.
Two change-listener paths + two snapshots in extension.ts — more wiring surface, and S003's truthful-sync/revert UX would then have to consume TWO engines.
Contradicts the HLD intent that every config-track story CONSUMES sc8 rather than standing up a sibling engine.
alternativesConsidered.reasonRejected: Matches a1 on ac1/ac2/k3/k7 but VIOLATES the sc8 contract intent and only PARTIALLY holds k5 by duplicating the truthful-apply engine — a real drift hazard S003 would then have to consume twice. Worse than a1 for the same user outcome.

alternativesConsidered.name: Single object-typed `insrc.models.tasks` blob setting
alternativesConsidered.oneLineSummary: Declare one machine-scoped object setting whose value is the whole roleId->tier override map as JSON; sc8 pulls config.show's models.tasks into it and writes changed leaves.
alternativesConsidered.approach: A single native setting `insrc.models.tasks` of JSON-schema type 'object' holds the entire per-role override map (roleId keys -> tier values). pullFromDaemon writes the daemon's models.tasks object into that one key; applyChanges deep-diffs the edited object against the snapshot and writes each changed roleId leaf via the segment-array config.write. No per-role manifest authoring — one key covers all roles, and a new role appears automatically.
pros: One manifest key, zero per-role authoring, no manifest-vs-catalog drift when the role registry grows.
Naturally represents 'no override' (absent object key) vs an explicit override without a default-equals-value ambiguity.
cons: Loses VS Code's native per-field editing entirely — the user hand-edits raw JSON with no enum dropdown / per-role tier validation / description, directly undercutting ac1's 'presented as an editable choice' (the same raw-JSON shape the spec + S001's a2 already ruled out for config editing).

Deep-diff a whole nested object per change with no per-field VS Code enum to lean on — more client-side work and more room for a subtle diff bug in the k5 path, and coreFloor/effective-tier display has nowhere native to render.
No validation that a value is a real tier until the client checks it — a fat-fingered JSON edit reaches the diff before rejection.
alternativesConsidered.reasonRejected: Violates ac1 by degrading per-role editing to raw JSON (no typed choice) and only partially holds sc8/k5 via a deep-diff; only ac2/k3/k7 hold. Its 'no default-ambiguity' advantage does not offset losing the native editable choice ac1 requires.

openQuestions: Remove-override-on-Reset: when the user Resets a per-role setting (or sets it equal to defaultTier), S002 leaves an explicit models.tasks.<roleId>=defaultTier override rather than DELETING the key (config.write sets, it does not delete). Behaviourally identical to no override but not a true removal; the delete-on-reset affordance is deferred to s3 or a later refinement.

sc8 extension confirmation: S002 adds two ADDITIVE methods to the S001-owned sc8 ConfigGateway (writeKeyPath, rawConfig) + two optional ConfigKeyEntry fields (segments, source) via a tracked sharedContract.methodAdd HLD amendment, realizing the per-role segmentation S001 explicitly deferred to S002. Confirm at approval that additively extending S001-owned sc8 is acceptable (vs an S001 back-flow).
